analysis: Both changed files are test-only Swift files: NativeBlockRetirementBridgeTests.swift (adds a TextSession fixture and the nativeBlockRequestsCarryNoStopScope test, head lines 50-71 and 92-117) and the new ReasoningStopScopeTests.swift. No production code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, cache storage or authorization path is changed, so no threat-model asset or trust boundary (TB-002, TB-007, TB-011, T-041) has a changed control in this batch. The tests document behavior of the stop-string scoping feature, which lives in production files outside the supplied units: reasoning and tool-call regions are excluded from stop matching, and the native block decoder ignores the scope and matches stops over the whole output. That native-block behavior is a functional and semantic matter. It is not a security regression, since the consumer controls its own stop strings and no cross-tenant data is involved. The tests use fixed in-memory fixtures with no secrets, network, filesystem or privileged operations. The remaining integration question is the production ReasoningStopScope, StopHoldback and CBv2StopStringScope implementation, which was not supplied. Whether it bounds memory for adversarial model output or stop strings (DoS) cannot be determined from these tests, and the tests themselves introduce no new attack surface.
